title: Tensor stability of the derived open test object
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an arbitrary open, with all derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] supplied in a common Hom universe. Let R be derived over restriction followed by Modules.overEquiv U [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], and use the shared derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. For B in D(O_X), assume R.map: Hom(B,E) → Hom(R(B),R(E)) is bijective for every E in D(O_X). Then R.map: Hom(B tensor L,E) → Hom(R(B tensor L),R(E)) is bijective for every L,E in D(O_X).

proof.text: For any adjunction J ⊣ R and object B, the right triangle identity identifies R.map on Hom(B,E) with the adjunction homEquiv after precomposition by the counit at B. Coyoneda therefore gives equivalence between bijectivity for every E and invertibility of the counit. Bijectivity is invariant under natural isomorphism of functors and postcomposition by a fully faithful functor. These are the proved private helpers hom_bijective_iff_counit and hom_bijective_natIso.

Use the open counit stalk formula: inside U the counit is an isomorphism on stalks; outside U its source is zero. Stalkwise detection of isomorphisms then identifies invertibility of the sheaf counit at F with zero stalks of F outside U. Exactness of extension and restriction identifies homology of the complex counit with the counit of each homology sheaf, by ShortComplex.homologyMap_mapNatTrans. Thus that complex counit is a quasi-isomorphism precisely when all cohomology stalks outside U vanish. Localize the termwise adjunction through DerivedCategory.Q using Adjunction.localization. Its counit on Q(P) is Q of the complex counit, conjugated by the factorization isomorphisms. Represent any B by a complex and transport its homology to obtain raw_derived_hom_support.

Choose K-flat resolutions P of a representative of B and J of a representative of L. Their augmentations supply isomorphisms Q(P) ≅ B and Q(J) ≅ L. Evaluate the K-flat first-variable tensor comparison on constant singleton families, using P K-flat, to identify B tensor L with Q(Tot(P tensor J)). Apply derived_tensor_stalk_vanishing using J K-flat and the assumed vanishing of cohomology stalks of B; transport zero stalks along the tensor comparison. This proves the private tensor_stalk_vanishing helper without a braiding argument.

Use mapDerivedCategoryCompIso for over restriction followed by Modules.overEquiv U. The derived functor of that equivalence is fully faithful, so its map on each Hom is bijective. Translate the hypothesis to raw over restriction, apply raw_derived_hom_support, then tensor_stalk_vanishing outside U, and apply raw_derived_hom_support in reverse for B tensor L. Finally transfer the resulting Hom bijection back through the derived equivalence. The empty and whole opens and zero factors require no additional assumptions.

theorem derivedOpen_tensorHom_bijective
    (X : Scheme.{uX}) (U : X.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ V : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    (B : schemeDerivedCategory X) :
    let R := ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U) ⋙
      Equivalence.functor
        (C := SheafOfModules.{uX} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
        (D := SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
        (Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory
    (∀ E : schemeDerivedCategory X,
      Function.Bijective (fun f : B ⟶ E ↦ R.map f)) →
    ∀ L E : schemeDerivedCategory X,
      Function.Bijective (fun f : B ⊗ L ⟶ E ↦ R.map f)
